speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. To begin my assessment, how many weeks pregnant was your mother when you were born, and were there any complications during delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (also known as Breastfeeding Jaundice or Suboptimal Intake Jaundice). The clinical picture of a well-appearing, term, exclusively breastfed infant with weight gain and progressive jaundice starting after the first week is classic for this benign condition caused by temporary milk supply不足 leading to reduced stooling and enterohepatic circulation of bilirubin.
